tier_justification: Folklore made precise. The conclusion is the situation that FZW16 describe as 'X ⋈ Y and X ⊕ Y ∈ bij-lens' and that AFP Optics assumes in locale `sym_lens`; it is also the two-location instance of the global-state theory of PP02. None of the sources checked derives it from PutGet, get-invariance in both directions and joint injectivity of the getters, or isolates that as an equivalent and irredundant law set. Not claimed novel.
plain_claim: For two total lenses l₁ : Lens S A and l₂ : Lens S B: if each satisfies PutGet, neither put changes the other's view (PutIndep in both directions), the two views together determine the state (JointExt), and S is nonempty whenever A × B is, then the specific map s ↦ (l₁.get s, l₂.get s) is a bijection S → A × B under which l₁.put is first-coordinate update and l₂.put is second-coordinate update; conversely, this conclusion implies all five laws and the nonemptiness condition. GetPut, PutPut and commuting puts are not assumed.

hypotheses.name: h₂ : PutGet l₂
hypotheses.purpose: l₂.put really stores the written value.

hypotheses.name: h₁₂ : PutIndep l₁ l₂

hypotheses.name: h₂₁ : PutIndep l₂ l₁
hypotheses.purpose: Frame law in the other direction; also what makes the base-state construction hit every pair.

hypotheses.purpose: No hidden state: injectivity of the pairing map.

Exactly the nonemptiness condition of the equivalence; implied by Nonempty S (pass `fun _ => hS`), but holds also when A × B is empty, e.g. for an empty state type with an empty view (Toy.Lens.emptyView_isProductDecomposition_without_nonempty).

hypotheses.name: S A B : arbitrary types in arbitrary universes
hypotheses.purpose: No finiteness or decidability is assumed, and no inhabitedness of S, A or B beyond hS; in particular the result applies when A or B is empty.

depth_note: Three of the four conjuncts of the unfolded conclusion restate hypotheses: injectivity of the pairing map is JointExt, and 'l₁.put is first-coordinate update' unfolds to PutGet l₁ ∧ PutIndep l₁ l₂ (Toy.Lens.isProductDecomposition_iff_elementary). The only non-definitional content is surjectivity: from a base state, put through l₁ and then through l₂. The converse direction is unfolding.
nonvacuity_witness: fst and snd on Bool × Bool (and on any product) satisfy all six hypotheses and the conclusion.
non_claims: The six hypotheses are sufficient (first Lean statement), jointly equivalent to the conclusion (second Lean statement) and irredundant (each has a counterexample in canonical form). The common stronger hypothesis `Nonempty S` implies `hS` but is not necessary: when A × B is empty the conclusion can hold on an empty state type (Toy.Lens.emptyView_isProductDecomposition_without_nonempty).

Does not constructively build an `Equiv S (A × B)` in `Type`: `hS` and `IsProductDecomposition l₁ l₂` live in `Prop`, so obtaining a computable inverse requires a concrete base state `s₀ : S` (see F1-inverse) or `Classical.choice`.

Does not apply to a proper subset of fields of a record with three or more fields (or hidden metadata/padding): `JointExt` fails whenever any unprojected state component exists; use F3-pair (with `VeryWellBehaved` and `PutComm`) or F2 over all fields instead.

Dropping `PutGet l₁`, `PutGet l₂`, `PutIndep l₁ l₂` or `PutIndep l₂ l₁` breaks the coordinate-update (`Intertwines`) part of `IsProductDecomposition`, not necessarily the bijectivity of `pairGet`: for ignorePut/snd, fst/ignorePutSnd and snd/twist (Toy.Lens.pairGet_bijective_in_inverse_witnesses) and for fst/xorView (Toy.Lens.xorView_pairGet_bijective_but_not_decomposition), `pairGet` is still a bijection.
The 'puts are coordinate updates' half of the conclusion carries no information beyond PutGet and PutIndep; see the depth note.

Attractive but inadequate weakening of the conclusion: 'some bijection S ≃ A × B exists'. A record with a ghost component admits such a bijection (Toy.Lens.ghost_admits_unrelated_bijection); the specific map must appear in the statement. Any map whose components are the two getters is `pairGet` (Toy.Lens.eq_pairGet_of_get_eq; each of its two hypotheses is needed: Toy.Lens.eq_pairGet_tight_left, Toy.Lens.eq_pairGet_tight_right).
Attractive but false variant of the hypotheses: both lenses very well-behaved, jointly extensional, and independent in one direction only (Toy.Lens.xorView_tight_putIndep_left).
Says nothing about partial lenses or sum types (see F5), about more than two fields (see F2), or about type-changing lenses.

tier_justification: Known result restated. PS03 Theorem 2.3.9 states it with no inhabitedness assumption (via the put-orbit construction), and CDV21 mechanise it in Agda for sources that are sets (`≃Σ∥set⁻¹∥×`, no inhabitedness assumption on the source or the view). What differs here is only the Lean formulation: the complement is required to live in the universe of S, where the quotient of S by 'put s = put t' provides one; the CDV21 complement is a subtype of the function type B → A.
plain_claim: A total lens l : Lens S A is very well-behaved if and only if it has a constant complement: a type C in the universe of S and a bijection S ≃ A × C under which get is the first projection and put is first-coordinate update. Neither S nor A is assumed nonempty.

hypotheses.purpose: Needed: without it no constant complement exists.

hypotheses.name: left-hand side, PutGet l
hypotheses.purpose: Needed: without it no constant complement exists.

hypotheses.purpose: Needed: without it no constant complement exists.

hypotheses.name: C : Type u (universe of S) inside HasConstantComplement
hypotheses.purpose: Lets the forward direction use the quotient construction; for complements in other universes the backward direction is F3-sharp.

depth_note: Backward: compute under the bijection and cancel it (F3-sharp). Forward: take C to be S modulo 'put s = put t', map s ↦ (get s, [s]) and (a, [s]) ↦ put s a; GetPut gives one inverse law, PutGet and PutPut the other.
nonvacuity_witness: fst on Bool × Bool (complement: the second field); the state-twisting lens (complement: a xor b).
non_claims: Does not imply that `l.get` is surjective when `S` is empty (with nonempty `A`, `VeryWellBehaved l` holds vacuously while `l.get : Empty → A` is not surjective; Toy.Lens.emptyState_veryWellBehaved_not_surjective).

The complement `C` is non-unique in two distinct senses: when `A` is inhabited, `C` is unique up to bijection (`C ≃ Fiber l a₀`) but the embedding/projection is not unique (e.g., `twist` splits with complement `a xor b` rather than `b`); when `A` is empty (hence `S` is empty), `C` is not even unique up to bijection (every `C : Type u` is a constant complement; Toy.Lens.emptyView_hasConstantComplement_any).

The backward direction of `HasConstantComplement` requires `C : Type u` (the universe of `S`); for a complement in an arbitrary universe `Type x`, use `veryWellBehaved_of_injective_intertwines_fst` (F3-sharp).
By the backward direction, any lens failing `GetPut`, `PutGet`, or `PutPut` has no constant complement at all; F3 gives no weaker decomposition for well-behaved lenses that fail `PutPut`.
Does not say that a very well-behaved put leaves a *given* sibling field alone: the complement is some type, not a prescribed field (Toy.Lens.twist_hasConstantComplement).
Says nothing about weaker put-put laws (JR12).

tier_justification: Known in other formalisms: JRW10 Proposition 9 (a very well behaved lens with getter g is exactly an algebra structure on g for a monad on Set/V, so for a fixed getter the puts are those algebra structures); Clarke20 Example 25 (a state-based lens is an internal lens between codiscrete categories whose Put part is a discrete opfibration, with GetPut and PutPut as the identity and composition laws of a functor); and CDV21 (a higher lens is a getter together with a proof that its family of fibres is coherently constant; higher lenses are equivalent to traditional lenses for types satisfying UIP). In categorical terms a coherent family of fibre maps is a functor from the codiscrete category on A to Set, whose category of elements is a discrete opfibration over that codiscrete category with object set S. The explicit set-level form with coherent fibre maps, the exposed constructions toPut/ofPut and the law-by-law correspondence, mechanised, was not found stated in the sources consulted.
plain_claim: Fix a getter get : S → A, and call a family of maps between the fibres of get (one map for every ordered pair of views) coherent if each fibre's map to itself is the identity and maps compose. Then the construction toPut (move a state to the fibre of the written view) sends every coherent family to a very well-behaved put for get, the construction ofPut (x ↦ put x a') sends every very well-behaved put to a coherent family, and ofPut undoes toPut on every family (toPut undoes ofPut by definition, Toy.Lens.toPut_ofPut), so coherent families and very well-behaved puts correspond bijectively. Law by law, for a put with PutGet, GetPut holds iff its fibre maps satisfy the identity law and PutPut holds iff they compose. (Each map of a coherent family is a bijection: the proved lemma Toy.Lens.FiberMaps.Coherent.leftInverse.)

hypotheses.name: get : S → A (arbitrary)
hypotheses.purpose: No inhabitedness or surjectivity assumption; for empty S or non-surjective get see the non-claims.

hypotheses.name: h : PutGet (Lens.mk get put) (law-by-law statement)
hypotheses.purpose: Needed to form ofPut (the maps must land in the fibres); a put without PutGet is not of the form toPut φ (Toy.Lens.toPut_putGet).

depth_note: Both directions are computations; the only subtle step is transporting a fibre element along an equality of views (get (put s a) = a) inside the dependent family.
nonvacuity_witness: For the first projection on Bool × Bool, the fibre maps of fst (and of the state-twisting lens) are coherent.
non_claims: Does not single out an intended put: for a fixed getter there are in general many very well-behaved puts (two for the first projection on Bool × Bool: Toy.Lens.fst_twist_two_veryWellBehaved_puts, Toy.Lens.veryWellBehaved_puts_getFst_eq_fst_or_twist); see F6-unique for the extra law that does.

Empty fibres: if one fibre is empty and another is not, there is no family of fibre maps and hence no very well-behaved put (Toy.Lens.fiberMaps_empty_of_empty_fiber); in particular, on an inhabited state type a put with PutGet forces get to be surjective (Toy.Lens.surjective_of_putGet_of_nonempty). On an empty state type there is exactly one put and it is very well-behaved, whatever A is (Toy.Lens.veryWellBehaved_put_unique_of_isEmpty).

Does not by itself say when a very well-behaved put exists; for an inhabited view type the base-fibre form (F6-count) shows that one exists exactly when every fibre is in bijection with the fibre over a base view.
The correspondence is between puts for one fixed getter; it does not classify lenses up to isomorphism of the state type.
toPut is also a bijection from all families of fibre maps (coherent or not) onto puts satisfying PutGet (third conjunct together with Toy.Lens.toPut_ofPut and Toy.Lens.toPut_putGet).

The two coherence conditions are independent and each is needed for very-well-behavedness: the fibre maps of the sibling-resetting setter satisfy map_comp (the setter satisfies PutPut, Toy.Lens.resetSibling_putPut) but not map_self (Toy.Lens.ofPut_resetSibling_not_coherent; the setter violates GetPut), and the fibre maps of the dirty-flag setter satisfy map_self (Toy.Lens.dirtyFlag_getPut) but not map_comp (Toy.Lens.ofPut_dirtyFlag_not_coherent; the induced put is not very well-behaved, Toy.Lens.toPut_ofPut_dirtyFlag_not_veryWellBehaved).

The categorical reading (coherent families as functors from the codiscrete category on A to Set, very well-behaved lenses as discrete opfibrations or delta lenses over codiscrete categories) is a correspondence with the literature, not a Lean statement of this package; no category theory is formalised here.

tier_justification: Follows from F6 by elementary counting; no source located that states the count.
plain_claim: Fix a getter get and a base view a₀: very well-behaved puts for get correspond bijectively to families of bijections from the fibre over a₀ to each other fibre, via put ↦ (x ↦ put x a). Consequently, if the view type has exactly k elements and every fibre of get has exactly m elements, the very well-behaved puts are in bijection with Fin (k − 1) → Equiv (Fin m) (Fin m) and there are exactly (m!)^(k − 1) of them (with truncated subtraction, also correct for k = 0).

hypotheses.name: a₀ : A (base-fibre form)
hypotheses.purpose: Base view; the base-fibre form is vacuous for empty A, which the counting form covers with k = 0.

hypotheses.name: hA : Nonempty (Equiv A (Fin k))
hypotheses.purpose: The number of views.

hypotheses.name: hF : ∀ a, Nonempty (Equiv (GetFiber get a) (Fin m))
hypotheses.purpose: Uniform fibre size; with non-uniform fibres there is no very well-behaved put.

depth_note: Base-fibre form (shallow): from a coherent family take the maps out of the fibre over a₀; conversely compose the bijections through the base fibre. Counting form (substantive without a library of finite cardinalities): transport along the given bijections and build an explicit bijection between the self-bijections of Fin m and Fin m!.
nonvacuity_witness: First projection on Bool × Bool: k = 2, m = 2, base view false; there are exactly 2 = 2!^1 very well-behaved puts (fst and twist).
non_claims: Counts puts for one fixed getter, not lenses up to isomorphism.
Only for finite view types and finite, uniform fibres; for non-uniform fibres the count is 0 (Toy.Lens.card_tight_uniform_fibers).
Says nothing about which of the (m!)^(k − 1) puts is intended; see F6-unique.

Edge case m = 0, k >= 1: for the empty state type with a nonempty finite view type every fibre has 0 elements and the formula gives (0!)^(k - 1) = 1, counting the unique (empty) put, which is very well-behaved even though get is not surjective (Toy.Lens.card_veryWellBehaved_puts_empty_state_two_views, instance k = 2). The count does not require get to be surjective.

Edge case k = 1: with a one-element view type the formula gives (m!)^0 = 1 for every fibre size m; the unique very well-behaved put is the write that changes nothing, put s a = s, forced by GetPut (Toy.Lens.veryWellBehaved_put_eq_self_of_subsingleton_view).

Both conclusions are propositions: `∃ e : Equiv ...` in the base-fibre form and `Nonempty (Equiv ...)` in the counting form live in Prop. The proofs use Classical.choice (to pick the fibre bijections given by hF, and a classical decidable equality on A when A has no DecidableEq instance); no computable enumeration of the very well-behaved puts is extracted.

tier_justification: Known: an update translation under a constant complement is unique once the complement is fixed (BS81, as recalled in FGMPS07 Section 10). Restated as a frame law against a complement view.
plain_claim: Fix get : S → A and a second lens m : Lens S C whose view together with get determines the state and such that every pair of values is realised. Then there is exactly one put for get that satisfies PutGet and leaves the m-view unchanged (the frame law PutIndep (Lens.mk get put) m), and it is very well-behaved.

hypotheses.name: hext : ∀ s t, get s = get t → m.get s = m.get t → s = t
hypotheses.purpose: The complement view and get together determine the state. Used for uniqueness (second conjunct) and for very-well-behavedness (third conjunct); dropping it breaks both: with a one-point complement view, fst and twist both satisfy PutGet and the frame law, and so do the dirty-flag setter (not PutPut) and the sibling-resetting setter (not GetPut).

hypotheses.name: hsurj : ∀ a c, ∃ s, get s = a ∧ m.get s = c
hypotheses.purpose: Every pair of values is realised; a sufficient condition used for existence (first conjunct). It is not necessary for the conclusion: see the non-claims.

hypotheses.name: m.put
hypotheses.purpose: Not used: only the getter of m matters.

depth_note: Existence: put s a is the state realising (a, m.get s) (choice). Uniqueness: two such states agree on both views. Very well-behaved: F1-laws' derived laws.
nonvacuity_witness: The first projection with complement view snd on Bool × Bool.
non_claims: PutGet, GetPut and PutPut alone do not determine the put (Toy.Lens.fst_twist_two_veryWellBehaved_puts: fst and twist have the same getter).

Which put is singled out depends on the complement view: with complement view snd it is fst.put; with the XOR view (which together with the first projection also determines the state) it is the state-twisting put, and fst.put violates the frame law (Toy.Lens.twist_putIndep_xorView_complement).
Does not assert that a complement view exists; by F3, one exists exactly for very well-behaved lenses.
With a complement view that does not determine the state (e.g. a one-point view), uniqueness fails (Toy.Lens.existsUnique_put_tight_jointExt).

Dropping hext breaks more than uniqueness: with the one-point complement view unitLensB on Bool × Bool (hsurj holds), the dirty-flag setter and the sibling-resetting setter satisfy PutGet and the frame law but violate PutPut and GetPut respectively, so the third conjunct fails too (Toy.Lens.existsUnique_put_drop_jointExt_admits_unlawful_puts).

hsurj is a sufficient condition, not a necessary one: for the identity getter on Bool with a constant complement view, hext holds and hsurj fails, yet there is exactly one put with PutGet and the frame law, and it is very well-behaved (Toy.Lens.existsUnique_put_hsurj_not_necessary). The exact existence condition, for any second view m, is `∀ s a, ∃ s', get s' = a ∧ m.get s' = m.get s` (Toy.Lens.exists_put_putGet_putIndep_iff).

The existence conjunct `∃ put, ...` lives in Prop and its proof uses Classical.choice; the theorem does not construct a computable put. A computable put needs an explicit function picking, for each (a, m.get s), the state realising it.
